title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
summary: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.

title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, Contribution to the proceedings of the International conference "Particle Physics at Medium and High Energies", June 2-5, 2026, Protvino, Russia
summary:
The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics
  where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron.
  Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.

title: Algebraic models of alpha-cluster nuclei
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, proceedings of Cluster26, to be published by Journal of Physics: Conference Series
summary: In this contribution I review the algebraic cluster model (ACM) for $α$-conjugate nuclei with $A=4n$ and its extension to the cluster shell model (CSM) for $A=4n+x$ nuclei. The CSM describes the splitting of single-particles levels in a deformed field generated by the cluster of $α$-particles. As an example, I discuss the energies, electromagnetic transitions and form factors of the neighboring nuclei $^{12}$C and $^{13}$C.

title: Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne--Ne collisions
summary: Nucleon-nucleon interactions within atomic nuclei give rise to collective properties such as deformation and nuclear clustering. Ultrarelativistic nucleon-nucleon collisions offer a novel way to probe the many-body correlations of the incoming nuclei, as the nuclear structure is reflected in the initial geometry of the produced system. State-of-the-art low-energy nuclear theory calculations predict highly deformed $^{20}$Ne nuclei with a characteristic $α$+$^{16}$O bowling-pin-like shape. Since such nuclei have recently been collided at the LHC, investigating methods to maximise the sensitivity to the nuclear structure is pertinent. In this paper, we investigate whether body--body and tip--tip configurations of $^{20}$Ne nuclei can be identified in Monte--Carlo Glauber simulations using geometry-sensitive observables: the eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and the transverse compactness, $d_\perp$. The nuclear configurations are obtained from nuclear lattice effective field theory calculations within the framework of Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and $\textit{ab initio}$ Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM). We utilise a Fisher linear discriminant to select body--body and tip--tip configurations based on the $\varepsilon_2$-$d_\perp$ correlation. With classifier thresholds chosen to retain $30\%$ of the target class in a validation sample, the two-variable Fisher selection obtains purities in NLEFT (PGCM) of $0.201$ ($0.156$) and $0.573$ ($0.540$) for body--body and tip--tip events, respectively.

title: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
comment: 33 pages, 9 figures. Code available at https://github.com/derek-teaney/DFHydro
summary: We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the Müller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.

title: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
summary: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.

title: Is XTE J1814-338 a dark matter-admixed neutron star?
summary: We explore the possibility that the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338 is a dark matter-admixed neutron star (DNS) based on a general-relativistic two-fluid approach, in which one fluid describes ordinary nuclear matter and the other dark matter. The equations of state of nuclear matter and dark matter are described by the Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) theory with realistic three-body forces and a generic bosonic self-interacting dark matter model, respectively. Based on the observational data, we determine the parameter space for XTE J1814-338 as a DNS, and find that only a halo stellar configuration with a high dark matter fraction is allowed. Furthermore, we predict other observable properties of XTE J1814-338 and provide robust lower bounds for these quantities.

title: The role of spin polarization in event-by-event fluctuations
summary: The event-by-event initial state fluctuations constitute a critical physical quantity for understanding the dynamics of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Due to the extremely limited available experimental data of such fluctuations, it is difficult to constrain or direct the characterization of the underlying initial state properties. This work constrains the correlation function between the initial eccentricity and the asymmetry by employing a parton distribution function that incorporates spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity and thermal shear. Based on the kinetic theory calculations, we found that the asymmetry fluctuations considering spin polarization have a significant splitting effect compared to those without spin polarization. These splitting exhibit pronounced system size and energy dependence. Moreover, the ratios of correlation function display similar system size and energy dependence--particularly in the low-temperature regime ($T \lesssim$ 0.12 GeV). These results suggest that spin polarization may serve as a useful constraint method for the event-by-event initial state fluctuations of heavy-ion collisions.
